title: Native MCP clients use exact callbacks and site-bound OAuth grants
steps: Run static callback and signed-out authorize cases for Claude Code, Cursor and Codex.
Submit Allow and Cancel in Chromium from an HTTPS consent page to actual loopback listeners.
With TEST_DATABASE_URL set to a disposable PostgreSQL database, run the MCP OAuth composition-root suite.
expect: Only each client’s registered callbacks reach sign-in; altered hosts, ports, paths, queries and other clients’ callbacks are rejected.
Both decisions arrive at the exact callback with state and issuer. Allow stores one site-bound code; Cancel stores none.

Authorization codes require S256, the exact stored callback, client and resource. Cross-client refresh/revoke cannot affect a connection. Rotation keeps the key id; revocation ends access and refresh; cross-site calls return 403.
fence: Fixed public client IDs and exact redirect lists; signed consent, S256 PKCE, resource/client/grant and single-site binding.

tests: native public clients accept only their exact callbacks without fetching metadata
native callback discovery reaches sign-in and binds the request to the exact client
native tracy-codex allow: browser follows CSP through to the exact loopback callback
